battle.name: 克里莫尼迪茲戰爭
battle.theater: 阿提卡半島與愛琴海南部
battle.brief: 公元前267至261年，馬其頓的安提柯二世與埃及的托勒密二世聯手，對抗塞琉古的安條克二世、斯巴達與埃托利亞聯盟；雅典由克里莫尼德斯率領加入，最後被海陸封鎖至公元前261年陷落。卡面的埃及月牙劍早於此役七百餘年退出一線，它留下的單刃彎砍邏輯落在聯軍色雷斯式 kopis 輕兵手上。

kit.name: 埃及月牙劍
kit.history: 外彎的單刃劍，砍下去不用拔。它比直劍更早出現在埃及人的手上。

countries: 克里莫尼迪茲戰爭爆發於公元前267年，交戰的是兩條互不相同的聯盟線。主攻方是馬其頓的安提柯二世·戈納塔斯與埃及的托勒密二世·費拉德爾弗斯，這一邊靠安提柯重新拉起來的科林斯同盟取得對希臘城邦發號施令的合法性，靠托勒密的錢糧與艦隊取得實力支撐；另一邊是塞琉古王國的安條克二世·提奧斯、埃托利亞聯盟、斯巴達，以及被推到台前來的雅典。安提柯方面的軍隊以馬其頓方陣為核心，混合伊利里亞與色雷斯的輕裝步兵、大量希臘雇傭兵，海軍是安提柯王朝自建的希臘式列槳戰艦；指揮系統以安提柯本人的近臣為中樞，外掛科林斯同盟會議的名義，行軍與戰役交給各級將領率領。托勒密方面以埃及步兵為基幹，疊上馬其頓式的方陣重裝步兵，艦隊由埃及、腓尼基與塞浦路斯水手組成，規模與財政都遠勝於聯軍；托勒密不親征，多以使者、金錢與一紙聯軍統帥授權指揮別人，這正是他介入希臘的方式。埃托利亞聯盟沒有常備國家軍隊，靠的是山地部落的民兵與雇傭兵，卻握有提爾斐、瑙派克托斯等地形與祭司集團的號召力；斯巴達出兵有限，重在象徵；雅典則是唯一有城牆、有海軍、有公民軍的城邦，卻缺錢缺船，只能靠外援。整體來看，這是一場不對稱的消耗戰：馬其頓與埃及握有制海權與現金，塞琉古與埃托利亞握有邊境游擊的空間，最後由哪一邊能把聯盟黏合起來決定勝負。
countriesEn: The Chremonidean War broke out in 267 BC between two very different alliance lines. The side on the offensive was Macedon under Antigonus II Gonatas and Egypt under Ptolemy II Philadelphus: the first drew its legitimacy to speak for the Greek cities from the League of Corinth that Antigonus had reconstituted, the second supplied the money, the grain and the warships. The other side was the Seleucid kingdom of Antiochus II Theos, the Aetolian League, Sparta, and the Athenians, who had been pushed to the front of the fighting. Antigonus's army was built around the Macedonian phalanx, mixed with Illyrian and Thracian light infantry and a large body of Greek mercenaries, and his navy consisted of the Greek-style oared galleys built in the Antigonid dockyards; command ran through the king's own close circle, wrapped in the authority of the League of Corinth, with campaigns and battles delegated to the generals. On the Ptolemaic side the backbone was Egyptian infantry, overlaid with Macedonian-style heavy phalanx troops, and the fleet was manned by Egyptian, Phoenician and Cypriot hands, far larger and far better paid than that of the allies; Ptolemy himself never came to Greece, and it was his envoys, treasurers and paymasters who held the coalition together, which was the standard way in which he intervened in Greek affairs. The Aetolian League had no standing national army, relying instead on the militia of the mountain clans and on mercenaries, yet it held the ground around Delphi and Naupactus and the authority of the priestly networks. Sparta sent limited forces and was largely symbolic, while Athens was the only polis that still possessed walls, a fleet and a citizen army, yet it lacked both money and ships and could only survive on outside aid. On the whole this was an asymmetric war of attrition: Macedon and Egypt held command of the sea and ready cash, the Seleucids and the Aetolians held room for guerrilla war, and the result was decided by which side could keep its alliance glued together.
people: 這場戰爭以雅典人克里莫尼德斯命名。他是雅典的將軍兼政治家，除留下悲劇與演說的記錄外，還在公元前263/262年前後由雅典議會通過的一道榮譽法令中被公開表彰：法令把金冠與一尊青銅像頒給克里莫尼德斯和他的同僚阿里斯塔爾科斯，理由寫得直白，說他們是為希臘人的自由而戰。這道法令是全場最重要的政治文件，因為它把安提柯二世用來打擊聯盟的口號反過來扣在安提柯頭上：聯盟才代表希臘的自由。戰場上最重要的對手是安提柯二世·戈納塔斯，他每一次遠征都包裝成解放，實則步步收緊希臘城邦的自主武力；計畫是先以海陸封鎖逼垮雅典，再等安條克二世的一次失敗遠征分散聯盟注意力，最後用圍城斷糧而不是會戰取勝。塞琉古王安條克二世·提奧斯在名義上是聯軍領袖，承諾以敘利亞艦隊進入愛琴海，卻因航程與準備耽誤始終未能與埃托利亞人會師，是整場戰爭裡最關鍵的失誤。埃托利亞方面的主要將領是斯科普斯，他率領聯盟在公元前263/262年打敗過馬其頓派出的遠征軍，維持了山區游擊的主動。托勒密二世本人沒有來希臘，他派出的使者、財務官與軍需官才是聯盟的黏合劑。真正把整場戰爭記錄下來的是史家波利比奧斯，他當年往來於安提柯的使團之間，書中大量引述埃托利亞史家阿利斯托美涅斯，使後人得以知道雅典陷落與科斯島海戰的細節；此外，雅典的德馬得斯在最後階段代表城邦與安提柯談判，議定了拆牆與更換當權者的條件。
peopleEn: The war takes its name from the Athenian Chremonides. He was a general and statesman of Athens, and besides the tragedies and the set speeches attributed to him he was publicly honoured by a decree of the Athenian council passed around 263/262 BC: the decree awarded a gold crown and a bronze statue to Chremonides and to his colleague Aristarchus, and its stated reason was blunt, that they had fought for the freedom of the Greeks. That decree is the most important political document of the whole war, because it turned Antigonus II Gonatas's own slogan against him: it was the coalition, not the king, that stood for the freedom of the Greeks. The most important opponent in the field was Antigonus II Gonatas himself. Every one of his expeditions was packaged as a liberation while in practice tightening the autonomy of the Greek cities; his plan was to break Athens by a land and sea blockade, to wait for a failed expedition by Antiochus II to pull the coalition apart, and to win by starving the city into surrender rather than by a set-piece battle. Antiochus II Theos of the Seleucid empire was the nominal leader of the coalition and had promised to bring a Syrian fleet into the Aegean, yet because of delays in sailing and in preparation he never joined up with the Aetolians, and that single failure is the most decisive error of the war. The leading Aetolian commander was Scopas, who led the League in defeating a Macedonian expedition in 263/262 BC and kept the initiative in the mountains. Ptolemy II himself never came to Greece; it was his envoys, treasurers and supply officers who kept the coalition together. The man who actually recorded the war was the historian Polybius, who moved with Antigonus's embassies and quoted the Aetolian historian Aristomenes at length, which is how the details of the fall of Athens and of the naval battle off Cos survived. At the last stage Demades spoke for Athens in the negotiations with Antigonus, and the terms settled there included the demolition of the walls and a change of government in the city.
kits: 卡面這把埃及月牙劍，是一把青銅單刃鐮刀形長劍，刃口開在弧線的內側，砍下去不必把刀從肉裡往回抽；柄端護手做成蓮花狀或生命符狀的舍德形，刃身帶脊，前段略寬。它的形制在埃及第二中間期出現，第十八、第十九王朝的埃及步兵把它與長矛、斧頭並列使用，第十八王朝的浮雕裡可以看見戴笠形頭盔的埃及步兵持月牙劍列陣的樣子。公元前267年的希臘戰場上，這把刀早已不是制式武器：埃及的實戰冷兵器早已換成長矛、斧頭與直刃短劍，晚期埃及與托勒密王朝前期所留下的月牙劍標本更接近儀仗與榮譽器物，而不是列陣的兵器。所以它在這場戰爭裡的位置，是托勒密王朝這一邊的古物：它屬於被希臘人接手後仍刻意保留的埃及王權象徵，被收進宮廷與神廟的器物譜系；而真正延續它的是曲刃的思路。戰役裡真正上陣的裝備是這些：托勒密方的埃及步兵裝備長矛、硬弓與短刀，方陣重步兵用薩里沙長矛、亞麻布鑲片胸甲、科林斯式頭盔與大圓盾；安提柯方以安提柯式方陣為核心，配色雷斯式小盾的輕裝步兵與標槍；埃托利亞民兵是投擲標槍加小型盾牌的散兵。海軍兩邊都是希臘式列槳戰艦，裝撞角、投擲石球與火盆，士兵用登艦斧與短劍；科斯島海戰之後，聯軍靠這些船把糧秣與援兵一批批送進薩羅尼克灣。安提柯的攻城器械，攻城塔、投石機與撞錘，則用來拆雅典的城牆與長牆，而不是用來攻破要塞。與卡面同源的彎刃，在希臘人的輕步兵手裡就是色雷斯式的 kopis 與 harpe，希臘語的 harpe 本身就是鐮刀的意思，那種砍擊不回抽的用法，正是月牙劍最早的設計目的。
kitsEn: The khopesh on this card is a bronze single-edged sickle-shaped longsword whose cutting edge lies on the inside of the curve, so that a stroke does not have to be pulled back out of the wound; the hilt ends in a lotus or ankh-shaped shed, the blade is ridged and slightly widened toward the front. The type appears in Egypt in the Second Intermediate Period, and infantry of the Eighteenth and Nineteenth Dynasties carried it alongside the spear and the axe; in Eighteenth Dynasty relief one can see Egyptian soldiers in their round helmets drawn up in formation holding khopesh. On a Greek battlefield of 267 BC this blade was long out of the line of service: the fighting cold weapons of Egypt had already passed to spear, axe and straight shortsword, and the surviving khopesh specimens of the Late Period and of early Ptolemaic Egypt are closer to ceremonial and honour pieces than to weapons of the line. Its place in this war, therefore, is on the Ptolemaic side of the ledger as an antiquity: one of the Egyptian royal symbols that the Greek inheritors deliberately kept, entered into the inventories of palace and temple, while it was the idea of the curved edge that truly survived. The gear that actually fought was this: the Egyptian infantry of Ptolemy carried spears, composite bows and short blades, while the phalanx troops used sarissa pikes, linen-plated linothorax body armour, Attic helmets and large round shields; Antigonus's side was built on the Antigonid phalanx with Thracian-style peltasts and javelins; the Aetolian militia fought as skirmishers with javelins and small shields. Both navies were Greek-style oared galleys fitted with rams, stone-throwers and fire-pots, and their soldiers used boarding axes and short swords; after the battle off Cos the coalition used those same ships to carry grain and reinforcements into the Saronic Gulf in batches. Antigonus's siege engines, the siege towers, stone-throwers and battering rams, were employed to break down the walls of Athens and the Long Walls rather than to assault a fortress. The curved blade of the same family as the card appears in Greek hands as the Thracian kopis and the harpe, the Greek word harpe meaning sickle, and the stroke that needs no pull-back is precisely the earliest design purpose of the khopesh.
tactics: 安提柯二世面對的問題，是聯盟裡每一支軍隊都想自己打，而聯盟本身沒有統一戰線。他的解法非常明確：不打會戰，用封鎖代替決戰。雅典處在阿提卡半島上，東面是愛琴海與薩羅尼克灣，只靠兩條地峽與希臘本土相連；安提柯的海軍在薩羅尼克灣巡弋，封住比雷埃夫斯港的出入，陸軍則控制通往博伊俄蒂亞與伊利里斯平原的地峽，把雅典變成一座沒有陸路援軍的孤城。圍城真正的武器是飢荒：城牆擋得住攻城塔，擋不住斷糧，於是配給一日日遞減，守軍與城市裡的武裝先被耗掉。安提柯把攻城主力擱在城牆之外而不是城牆之上，寧可花時間維持封鎖，也不願在城下碰硬骨頭；只有當他確認城內撐不住時，才以有限度的進攻逼出一份能對全希臘交代的協議。埃托利亞人完全相反，他們不打會戰，只打地峽與山道：公元前263/262年，安提柯派出的遠征軍在埃托利亞境內被引入峽谷，後路被切斷而崩潰，安提柯為此折損一批兵力，也丟掉對提爾斐與安菲薩的控制，之後才重新奪回安菲薩。托勒密這邊的戰術，是用錢維持聯盟、用船維持補給線、把時間當武器：他不急著把援軍送入雅典，而是先在科斯島外海與安提柯的海軍較量，確保海上通道不斷，讓聯盟的糧秣與援兵可以持續抵達薩羅尼克灣。科斯島海戰本身是典型的希臘式海戰：兩列戰艦平行對列，盡量把船舷側對敵舷，靠撞角撞出裂口，投擲石球與火盆延燒船板，再由輕裝步兵跳舷登船；托勒密方多民族水手在近海纏鬥中的分隊編制佔了便宜。安條克二世那支本應改變戰局的敘利亞艦隊，因為遠航與協同失誤，始終沒有出現在愛琴海，聯盟的包圍圈因此永遠合不攏。整體而言，這是一場把會戰壓成消耗、把攻城壓成圍困、把海戰壓成補給線保衛戰的戰役。
tacticsEn: The problem facing Antigonus II was that every army in the coalition wanted to fight on its own account, while the coalition itself had no united front. His answer was unmistakable: no set-piece battle, blockade in place of decision. Athens sits on the peninsula of Attica, with the Aegean and the Saronic Gulf to the east, joined to the Greek mainland by only two isthmuses; Antigonus's navy patrolled the Saronic Gulf and closed the entrances to the Piraeus, while his land forces held the isthmuses leading to Boeotia and the Thriasian plain, turning Athens into a city cut off from land reinforcement. The real weapon of a siege was hunger: a wall stops a siege tower, but it does not stop a cut in the grain supply, and so the rations shrank day by day, wearing out the garrison and the armed citizens of the city first. Antigonus kept the bulk of his siege force outside the walls rather than against them, willing to spend time maintaining the blockade rather than risk a collision on the walls; only when he was sure the city could hold out no longer did he apply limited pressure to force out a settlement he could present to the whole of Greece. The Aetolians were the exact opposite: they avoided pitched battle and fought instead over passes and mountain tracks. In 263/262 BC a Macedonian expedition was drawn into a defile inside Aetolian territory, cut off behind, and destroyed, and Antigonus paid for this with troops and with control of Delphi and Amphissa, only to take Amphissa back later. The Ptolemaic tactic was to keep the alliance alive with money, keep the supply line alive with ships, and use time as the weapon: he was in no hurry to push reinforcements into Athens, but first measured his navy against Antigonus's in the water off Cos, so that the sea route stayed open and grain and reinforcements could keep reaching the Saronic Gulf. The battle off Cos was a textbook Greek naval action: two lines of galleys sailing parallel, trying to bring their flanks against the enemy's, opening the hulls with rams, setting fire to the decks with stones and fire-pots, and then sending light infantry across to board; the multi-national crews and the squadron organisation of the Ptolemaic fleet told in the close fighting of the narrow water. The Syrian fleet that should have changed the course of the war never appeared in the Aegean, because of the long voyage and the failure to coordinate, and the circle around Athens could therefore never be closed. In the end this was a campaign that compressed set-piece battle into attrition, siege into blockade, and naval battle into the defence of a supply line.
data: 幾個可以對照的數字：戰爭自公元前267年打到公元前261年，前後約六年，其中決定性的圍城發生在公元前262/261年，時間大約一年，史家沒有留下確切的日數。雅典的城防結構是可以量的：連接雅典城與比雷埃夫斯港的兩道長牆，單道長度約在六到七公里上下，兩道合計十公里左右，這是阿提卡防禦的骨幹，也是安提柯必須拿到海峽而不能只靠陸軍包圍的原因。科斯島在愛琴海東南部，距雅典約四百公里，聯軍的援軍與糧船要走完這段海程才能左右雅典的局勢；安提柯若要徹底切斷這條線，就必須先把海拿到手，於是科斯島海戰不是旁支，而是主戰場。安提柯二世在位的二十多年裡靠科林斯同盟的框架作戰，同盟名下的城邦數以數十計；托勒密二世一方常被描述為當時地中海最富的王朝，埃及的穀物、尼羅河的稅收與地中海的商業網，是聯盟津貼的來源。安提柯這邊則長期依賴雇傭兵：伊利里亞與色雷斯的步兵、希臘的方陣傭兵，每一場戰役都要重新募集與付款，一旦戰線拉長、錢不夠，士氣與戰力就同步下滑，這一點最終讓他的封鎖戰變成曠日持久的消耗。埃托利亞聯盟沒有常備軍與國庫，作戰能力受制於山區的冬季與部落的應徵意願，這解釋了它為何能以小兵力拖住馬其頓，也解釋了它為何不能把馬其頓從雅典趕走。兵力與傷亡方面，古代史料只給出概數：科斯島海戰的參戰艦船是數十艘的量級，波利比奧斯提到雙方的損失與俘虜，但都是概數而非帳冊；至於雅典全城人口與圍城期間的死亡數字，史料只以饑荒與大量死者無人收葬一類的說法帶過，沒有可核的數字。唯一有明確量級意味的，是長牆與城牆被拆之後雅典從此不再有可守的城防，以及聯盟在公元前261年被拆散之後，希臘城邦失去了集結兵力的制度框架。
dataEn: A few figures for comparison. The war ran from 267 to 261 BC, about six years in all, and the decisive siege fell in 262/261 BC and lasted roughly a year; the historians give no exact number of days. The defences of Athens can be measured: the two Long Walls that joined the city of Athens to the harbour of the Piraeus were each on the order of six to seven kilometres, roughly ten kilometres together, and they were the backbone of the defence of Attica as well as the reason why Antigonus needed the sea and could not rely on a land investment alone. Cos lies in the south-east Aegean, some four hundred kilometres from Athens, and the coalition's reinforcements and grain ships had to cover that sea distance before they could affect the situation inside the city; to cut that line completely Antigonus had to win the sea first, which is why the battle off Cos was no side-show but the main theatre. Antigonus II fought through the framework of the League of Corinth throughout his more than twenty years on the throne, with a number of member cities running into the tens; the Ptolemaic kingdom under Ptolemy II is regularly described as the richest court in the Mediterranean of its day, and the grain of Egypt, the revenues of the Nile and the commercial network of the eastern Mediterranean were the source of the coalition's subsidies. Antigonus's side, by contrast, leaned on mercenaries throughout, Illyrian and Thracian infantry and Greek phalanx troops, who had to be mustered and paid afresh for every engagement; once the front stretched and the money ran short, morale and fighting strength fell together, and that is what finally turned his blockade into an open-ended grind. The Aetolian League had no standing army and no treasury, and its fighting capacity was limited by the winter in the mountains and by the willingness of the clans to muster, which explains both how it could hold a Macedonian army at bay with small forces and why it could never drive the Macedonians away from Athens. On numbers of troops and casualties the ancient record gives only approximations: the fleets engaged off Cos were on the order of a few dozen galleys, and Polybius refers to losses and prisoners on both sides, but in general terms rather than as a ledger; the population of Athens and the number of dead during the siege appear in the sources only through the language of famine and of the many dead left unburied, with no verifiable figure. The only thing measured with real consequence is the demolition of the Long Walls and the circuit walls, after which Athens had no defensible fortification left, and the break-up of the coalition in 261 BC, after which the Greek cities no longer possessed any institutional framework for mustering troops.
cause: 這場戰爭的第一因，是安提柯二世把馬其頓的霸權重新包裝成科林斯同盟的合法秩序：公元前277年之後，希臘城邦在名義上獲得自由，實際上是安提柯的同盟城邦，這套說法要維持，就必須不斷削弱城邦的自主武力。雅典之所以成為抵抗的核心，是因為它是唯一還保有城牆、海軍與公民軍的城邦；但雅典自己也已在消耗戰裡透支，城牆在公元前338/337年之後修過，公民作戰的傳統卻一代比一代稀薄，土地兼併又讓兵源與稅基同時變薄。於是克里莫尼德斯這一批人選擇引外援：他們與埃托利亞人、斯巴達人一起向托勒密二世靠攏，換取津貼與艦隊，把保衛希臘說成聯盟的共同事業。第二個推力在埃及：安條克二世娶了托勒密一世的女兒貝蕾妮絲，兩人婚後的離婚與再婚風波，讓敘利亞與埃及在繼承權上的糾紛升溫；托勒密二世需要一個能牽制安條克、而自己不必下場的前線，雅典的聯盟正好符合這個需求。第三個推力在埃托利亞：聯盟與馬其頓在瑙派克托斯、提爾斐與安菲薩一帶的爭奪，直接把安條克的艦隊拉了進來，於是原本互不相干的矛盾湊成了一場大戰。第四個推力是安條克二世的承諾：他答應以敘利亞海軍援助聯軍，讓計畫看起來完整，而正是這支沒有及時趕到的艦隊，讓聯盟在最需要它的時候散了架。歸根到底，克里莫尼迪茲戰爭是亞歷山大帝死後繼承者們在希臘身上爭奪地盤的一場戰爭：安提柯要的是城邦的服從，托勒密要的是削弱塞琉古，埃托利亞要的是山地與商路的自主，雅典要的是那條已經守不住的自由防線，而安條克要的是把希臘的注意力從敘利亞拉回來。
causeEn: The first cause of this war was that Antigonus II repackaged Macedonian hegemony as the legal order of the League of Corinth: after 277 BC the Greek cities nominally enjoyed freedom while in fact they were the member cities of Antigonus, and such a story could only be maintained by steadily stripping the cities of the means to act on their own. Athens became the core of the resistance because it was the only polis that still kept walls, a fleet and a citizen army; but Athens too had been hollowed out by its own wars, its walls repaired after 338/337 BC while the tradition of the citizen soldier thinned out generation by generation, and the concentration of land shrank the pool of recruits and the tax base at the same time. So the men around Chremonides chose to bring in foreign help: they turned to Ptolemy II together with the Aetolians and the Spartans, trading his subsidies and his warships for the language of a common cause, the defence of the Greeks. The second push came from Egypt: Antiochus II had married Berenice, a daughter of Ptolemy I, and the divorce and remarriage that followed the marriage put the succession rivalry between Syria and Egypt on a sharper edge; Ptolemy II needed a forward position that could pin down Antiochus without his having to fight it in person, and the Athenian coalition fitted that need exactly. The third push came from Aetolia: the struggle between the League and Macedon over Naupactus, Delphi and Amphissa pulled Antiochus's fleet in directly, so that separate quarrels merged into one war. The fourth push was Antiochus's own promise: he undertook to bring a Syrian fleet to aid the coalition, which made the plan look complete, and it was precisely that fleet, arriving too late, that left the coalition falling apart at the moment it was needed most. In the end the Chremonidean War was a fight over Greece between the successors of Alexander the Great: Antigonus wanted the obedience of the cities, Ptolemy wanted the Seleucids weakened, the Aetolians wanted autonomy in the mountains and on the trade routes, Athens wanted a free defence it could no longer hold, and Antiochus wanted Greek attention pulled back from Syria.
impact: 公元前261年雅典陷落，是這場戰爭在希臘留下的最重刻痕。城牆與長牆被拆，雅典從此不再是能以城自守的城邦，公民軍的傳統也就此斷裂；城邦的民主運作被一批主張與安提柯合作的溫和派取代，希臘人自己的政治言論開始把雅典的失敗說成政策錯誤而不是力量不足。第二次雅典同盟在實質上解體，希臘城邦聯合自保的制度嘗試告一段落，這也是聯盟這個詞在後來兩千年裡與安提柯的秩序長期糾纏的起點。對埃及與馬其頓而言，這場勝利換來了實惠：托勒密保住了海軍與埃及的金流，安提柯則得到一座沒有城牆、沒有海軍、只能靠他保護的雅典，以及對提爾斐與安菲薩的控制，安提柯王朝對希臘本土的霸權因此確立並維持了數十年，直到公元前221年馬其頓在義大利戰敗、希臘被羅馬接管才告終。對塞琉古而言，這一戰沒有致命損失，卻讓安條克二世看到希臘聯盟靠不住，兩家的冷戰隨即在敘利亞與基埃斯商路上攤開，公元前260年之後的第三次敘利亞戰爭再起；托勒密二世趁勢收復科埃勒敘利亞，直到安條克二世在公元前246年去世，塞琉古才被迫收手。對托勒密王朝而言，這套用錢買希臘的自由、讓安提柯替自己消耗的做法，被後來的國王照抄：安提柯二世直到公元前238年在奇奧斯附近的海戰裡陣亡，聯盟的框架仍然有效，埃及出錢、馬其頓出兵的交換也一直延續到公元前3世紀末。安提柯王朝在奇奧斯海戰的敗亡，等於宣告這場戰爭的勝負在長時間尺度上並沒有定論：安提柯贏了雅典，卻輸了埃托利亞的游擊，最後連自己的王朝都沒能保住。
impactEn: The fall of Athens in 261 BC left the deepest mark of the war in Greece. The circuit walls and the Long Walls were pulled down; Athens was from then on a polis that could no longer defend itself by standing behind walls, and the tradition of the citizen army was broken with them; the working of the democracy was taken over by a group of moderates who argued for accommodation with Antigonus, and Greek political argument itself began to explain the defeat of Athens as a mistake of policy rather than a want of strength. The Second Athenian League was dissolved in substance, and the attempt of the Greek cities to guarantee their survival by standing together ended with it; this is where the long entanglement of the word league with the Antigonid order begins. For Egypt and Macedon the victory brought solid gain: Ptolemy kept his fleet and the flow of Egyptian money, and Antigonus gained a city without walls and without a fleet that could only look to him for protection, together with control of Delphi and Amphissa; the hegemony of the Antigonid dynasty over the Greek mainland was thus established and held for decades, until the defeat of Macedon in Italy in 221 BC and the Roman takeover of Greece. For the Seleucids the war cost nothing decisive, but it showed Antiochus II that the Greek coalition could not be relied on, and the cold war between the two houses reopened along the Syrian and Cilician routes, with the Third Syrian War breaking out after 260 BC; Ptolemy II took back Coele-Syria in the process, and only the death of Antiochus II in 246 BC forced the Seleucids to give way. For the Ptolemaic kingdom the method of buying Greek freedom with money and letting Antigonus do the wearing out was copied by the kings who followed: the coalition framework was still in place when Antigonus II fell in a naval battle off Chios in 238 BC, and the exchange of Egyptian money for Macedonian soldiers ran on into the late third century. The destruction of the Antigonid dynasty in that battle amounts to a verdict that the war was never finally decided on the long run: Antigonus won Athens, lost the Aetolian war of movement, and could not even keep his own dynasty.
result: 公元前261年，雅典的城門在封鎖與饑荒之後打開，德馬得斯代表的城邦與安提柯二世議定條件：拆毀城牆與長牆，接受安提柯的同盟秩序，城邦自治的軍事工具被解除。聯盟就此瓦解：埃托利亞在安條克的敘利亞艦隊未到之前先行退讓，雅典失去了最重要的盟友，斯巴達本來就出兵有限。托勒密二世沒有達成他最想達成的目標，安條克二世既沒有被削弱，也沒有被逐出小亞細亞；但他保住了海軍與制海權，聯盟的海上補給線在科斯島海戰之後仍然通著，使雅典的守軍撐到了最後，也讓托勒密在往後的第三次敘利亞戰爭中仍能以海軍切斷敘利亞沿岸的補給。安提柯二世在希臘獲得了最高的戰術成果：城邦聯盟的框架、提爾斐與安菲薩的控制，以及一座沒有城牆的雅典；之後他以此為基地，把馬其頓的影響推過整個希臘，在公元前261年之後的十數年間讓科林斯同盟成為地中海東岸秩序的代名詞。戰爭的直接結束點，是安提柯與塞琉古在公元前261/260年前後達成的休戰，以及托勒密與安條克在公元前259/258年簽訂的和約：貝蕾妮絲被送回埃及，敘利亞放棄對科埃勒敘利亞的爭奪，第三次敘利亞戰爭由此埋下伏線。往後看，這場戰爭留下的兩個制度性結果都極為長久：一是聯盟作為希臘城邦的戰爭機器被證明脆弱，羅馬人日後在第二次馬其頓戰爭中用同樣的名義、不同的手法收編了它；二是托勒密王朝證明了以錢買自由這條路可以在地中海東部長期運作，讓之後一個多世紀的希臘戰爭都帶著這條影子。
resultEn: In 261 BC the gates of Athens opened after the blockade and the famine, and the polis, represented by Demades, settled its terms with Antigonus II: the circuit walls and the Long Walls were to be demolished, the Antigonid order of the league accepted, and the military instruments of civic autonomy stripped away. The coalition came apart with them: the Aetolians gave ground before the Syrian fleet of Antiochus ever arrived, Athens lost its most important ally, and Sparta had never committed much in the first place. Ptolemy II did not obtain the outcome he most wanted, since Antiochus II was neither weakened nor driven out of Asia Minor; but he kept his fleet and command of the sea, and the maritime supply line of the coalition still ran after the battle off Cos, which carried the garrison of Athens to the end and allowed Ptolemy in the later Third Syrian War to cut the coastal supply of Syria with his navy. Antigonus II gained the highest tactical prize in Greece: the framework of the league of cities, control of Delphi and Amphissa, and an Athens without walls; from that base he carried the Macedonian influence across the whole of Greece, and for the decade and more after 261 BC the League of Corinth became the byword for the order of the eastern Mediterranean. The immediate end of the war came with the truce between Antigonus and the Seleucids around 261/260 BC and the treaty between Ptolemy and Antiochus in 259/258 BC: Berenice was sent back to Egypt, Syria gave up its claim on Coele-Syria, and the Third Syrian War was thereby set in motion. Looking further ahead, the two institutional results of this war proved exceedingly durable: first, the league proved fragile as a war machine of the Greek cities, and the Romans later absorbed the same institution in the Second Macedonian War under the same name and by very different methods; second, the Ptolemaic kingdom demonstrated that the road of buying freedom with money could be worked for the long run in the eastern Mediterranean, and that shadow hung over a century and more of Greek warfare.
